title: Find the Best Consecutive Product Group
real_world_story: A shopping platform displays products in a ranked sequence and wants to identify a consecutive group of products whose total price is closest to a customer's preferred spending amount.
problem_statement: Given an array of positive product prices, a window size K, and a target value T, find the consecutive group of K products whose total price is closest to T. Return the starting index of that group.
task: Find the K consecutive products whose combined price is closest to the customer's preferred spending amount.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and K. The second line contains N integers representing product prices. The third line contains an integer T representing the target spending amount.
output_format: Print the zero-based starting index of the K-product group whose sum is closest to T. If multiple groups have the same difference, return the smallest starting index.

examples.explanation: The group starting at index 1 contains 400, 500 and 700, whose total is exactly 1600.
The group starting at index 2 contains 700 and 800, whose total is 1500. This is the closest group to the target of 1200.

expected_algorithm.name: Sliding Window
expected_algorithm.reason: Because the products form consecutive groups of a fixed size, a sliding window can update each group sum efficiently.

hint: Calculate the sum of the first K products.
Slide the window one position at a time.
Remove the outgoing price and add the incoming price.
real_world_takeaway: Sliding windows are useful when recommendation systems need to evaluate consecutive groups of items efficiently.
